questions.q: In this lab's ticket, why does a Scheduled Job become the first suspect rather than a Business Rule?
options: SLA breach evaluation is a sweep-many-records-on-a-timer task, not something triggered by one record edit
Business Rules cannot affect SLA records under any circumstance
Scheduled Jobs are always the cause of any reported delay
The ticket explicitly states a Business Rule was recently deleted
questions.explain: Breach warnings arriving late points to a timer-driven sweep job, matching the Scheduled Job pattern from Lesson 26, not a single-record-event Business Rule.

questions.q: What is the second thing this lab checks, after a relevant System Property, and before opening any log?
options: The user's role assignments
The Scheduled Job's run history and Next action field
The Service Catalog variable set
The notification email template
questions.explain: After the property, the lab moves to the Scheduled Job record itself — checking Next action and run history to see if runs are falling behind schedule.

questions.q: What makes a job "fall behind" its own schedule, per this lab's example?
options: The job is disabled
The job is configured to run every 5 minutes but each run now takes 25 minutes to complete
The job's role requirement was removed
The job was deleted from sysauto_script
questions.explain: A job that takes longer to run than the gap between its own scheduled runs backs up exactly like the ticket's symptom, without failing outright.

questions.q: How does this lab use a run's start and end time once it has them from the job's history?
options: To delete old log entries covering that time range
To filter the System Log to that window, following the reproduce-then-check-timestamp workflow from Lesson 27
To change the job's role requirement
To create a new System Property
questions.explain: A specific run's timestamp anchors the System Log search so you're not scanning unrelated entries across the whole table.

questions.q: If the evidence shows the job's record volume genuinely grew and each run simply takes longer now, what is the real fix per this lab?
options: Rewrite the job's script from scratch regardless of the evidence
Adjust the job's interval or batch size, or escalate a capacity question — not assume the script is broken
Disable the job permanently
Grant the fulfiller the security_admin role
questions.explain: A job that's correctly working but outpaced by growing volume needs a scheduling or capacity fix, not a script rewrite assumed from the start.
